description: A full working week for an engineering manager with four real pending items whose stakes are ordered almost exactly opposite to their volume and urgency of tone. Tests ranking across a realistic manager's mixed inbox: a person problem, a budget deadline, a hiring decision, and a low-stakes process chore.

events.text: Reminder: 4 of your reports have not logged a Q3 goal. Managers must confirm goal entry in the tool by the end of the quarter.

events.text: Morgan, writing this at the end of the day so I don't say it badly in person. I've been offered a role elsewhere and I have to respond by the 18th. I don't especially want to leave, but I've been doing on-call for the billing consumers alone since May and nobody has picked up the second rotation slot. I'd like half an hour with you this week before I answer them. Please don't discuss it in the channel.
The staging cluster keeps evicting pods during the nightly load test. I think our memory limits are set from last year's traffic.
Almost certainly. I'll raise them and rerun tonight. No decision needed from anyone, it's a config change.

We need the vendor renewal line for the observability contract and confirmation of whether the second SRE requisition stays open. Submissions close Friday the 11th at 17:00; after that the numbers are locked for the quarter and changes need a re-forecast, which realistically means January.

@morgan-lu the panel for the senior SRE candidate is split two-two. As hiring manager you're the tiebreak. She has another offer with a deadline of the 16th, so I need your decision by the 15th at the latest.
Reminder: 4 of your reports have not logged a Q3 goal. This is the third reminder.

Good week overall — no incidents, load test green, and the migration runbook is finally written.

ground_truth.notes: Four genuine items, and the ordering is the test. The goal-entry chore generates three loud, repetitive bot reminders and is by far the least consequential; the retention conversation arrives once, quietly, in an email the sender explicitly asks not to broadcast, and is the item where delay is irreversible. Budget and hiring both carry hard external dates and sit in between. A briefing that leads with the bot reminders because they are numerous, or that leads with the budget because it has the nearest deadline, is a ranking failure — Friday's budget is recoverable by a January re-forecast, whereas Dev answering the offer is not. The staging thread is the precision counterweight: a real problem, opened and closed inside the window by someone else, explicitly needing no decision. Note also the confidentiality request — a correct briefing may state the item to its owner, since that is the whole point of a private briefing, but must not suggest raising it in the channel.
